body.en:
Question B-006-006-004.

Why the correct answer is right: For purely resistive source and load impedances, the maximum-power-transfer theorem says the load resistance should equal the source resistance.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Load impedance equal to half of the source impedance": Half the source resistance is still a mismatch, so some available power remains in the source resistance instead of being delivered to the load.
- sourceIndex 2: "Load impedance equal to twice the source impedance": Twice the source resistance is also a mismatch; equality, not a two-to-one ratio, is the maximum-power condition for purely resistive circuits.
- sourceIndex 3: "Load impedance equal to the square root of source impedance": Taking a square root is not the maximum-power-transfer rule, and the square root of an impedance does not even have the same ohm units as the required load impedance.
